failingTests: task 1: the login form signs in on success and reports wrong credentials
task 2: signed-in requests carry the bearer token
task 3: protected pages redirect to login and return after sign-in
task 4: admin screens and controls follow the signed-in role
task 5: a 401 clears the session and returns to login with an explanation
task 6: a 403 shows a not-allowed message without signing the user out
task 7: signing out forgets the session and guards the pages again
task 8: the dev auto-sign-in is off and the API address comes from the environment

cleanup.notes: Setup (npm ci in tests/) creates tests/node_modules; the optional dev setup (npm ci in starter/) creates starter/node_modules. Cleanup deletes both; the tests create nothing else. The tests stub fetch and never use the network; the dev server's mock API is local. The mock accounts, passwords and tokens (avery/beacon1, omar/beacon2, tok-avery, tok-omar) are fake development fixtures, not secrets. The session is kept in React state only; nothing is written to browser storage. Resetting the learner's work means restoring starter/src from a fresh copy of the lab. The expected output file writes variable timings as <ms>, and test file lines may print in any order. The 25-minute median and 30-minute cap are planning figures for the module's S34 guided lab slot, not a measured learner pilot. Setup (the one-time npm ci) completes before the lab slot's working time; the 30-minute allowance covers only work on the tasks. The two review topics are claimed only where a test scores them. Partial-objective note: javascript-fundamentals-review#o2 is scored for tracing awaited fetch calls and turning non-2xx responses into status-carrying errors in authFetch, LoginPage and handleRestart (tests 1, 2 and 6). Partial-objective note: react-review#o1 is scored for state, context, routing (Navigate and location.state) and form submission applied together, and for the state-update and changed-context-value re-render triggers (tests 1, 3, 6 and 7); effects and the parent-re-render trigger appear only in given code and are not scored. javascript-fundamentals-review#o1 (destructuring, spread, arrow functions, map and filter) and #o3 (ES module import and export) are not claimed: no task makes the learner write them. react-review#o2 (bug-class diagnosis) is deliberately not claimed by this lab; the react-review topic page practises it. Partial-objective note: turning-off-the-dev-profile#o2 is scored here only for its Vite-environment-variable clause (plus the front-end auto-sign-in twin); the Spring-profile clause is practised on the topic page, not in this lab. Partial-objective note: handling-401-and-403-redirect-and-sign-out#o1 is scored for applying the contract (401 means sign in again, 403 keeps the session and shows not-allowed; tests 5 and 6); stating the general HTTP meanings stays on the topic page. Partial-objective note: handling-401-and-403-redirect-and-sign-out#o2 is scored for clearing the client's auth state and returning to the login page and then the remembered page (tests 5 and 6), partly through given code (sessionExpired and use-authed-fetch.js); distinguishing this from the server ending an HttpOnly cookie session is practised on the topic page only. Partial-objective note: turning-off-the-dev-profile#o3 is scored by test 8 sending an unauthenticated request and the front end handling 401s (tests 5 and 6), verified against the stubbed secured API, not a real Spring back end. All assertions are behavioral through Testing Library against rendered output and the recorded fetch calls; no test reads the learner's source text.
